title: An efficient protocol to use feedback-controlling digital microfluidic fluorimetric sensor for detection of mercury (II) in coastal seawaters
author: Han, Liu, et al.
materials: Step2: Each droplet was identified and located.

steps.title: Mount DMF chip on holder
steps.instruction: Place the digital microfluidic (DMF) chip—two parallel plates measuring 63 × 33 mm with 24 patterned bottom electrodes—onto the chip holder and connect it to the control‑electronics PCB.

steps.title: Initialize control system and feedback
steps.instruction: Power on the control system; the FPGA scans the capacitance of each electrode using an oscillator that outputs variable‑frequency pulses, switching between voltage‑actuation mode and droplet‑sensing mode. The frequency data are sent to the computer for real‑time droplet position computation and feedback to the DMF chip.

steps.title: Dispense probe and sample droplets
steps.instruction: Load the mercury fluorescence probe (prepared in CH₃CN) onto its reservoir electrode and load each seawater sample onto its reservoir electrode. Dispense a 1 µL probe droplet and a 1 µL sample droplet from the respective reservoirs (up to three samples can be loaded simultaneously).

steps.title: Identify droplets and plan routing
steps.instruction: Using the control software, identify the position of each dispensed droplet, then generate a droplet‑routing plan that will merge, actively mix, and transport the droplets via EWOD actuation.

steps.title: Merge and actively mix droplets
steps.instruction: Move the 1 µL probe droplet and the 1 µL sample droplet to adjacent electrodes, merge them, and perform active mixing by applying reciprocating motion between the electrodes until the fluorescent reaction is complete (the total detection time is <20 s).

steps.title: Transfer to detection and capture image
steps.instruction: Transport the mixed droplet to the designated detection position, capture fluorescence images with a CCD camera mounted on a fluorescence microscope, and convert the images to eight‑bit grayscale using Image‑Pro Plus (Version 6.0 for Windows XP, Media Cybernetics, Inc.).

steps.title: Discard used droplet
steps.instruction: Move the droplet from the detection area to the waste‑reservoir electrode and discard it.

steps.title: Perform evaporation‑concentration pretreatment (optional)
steps.instruction: If the mercury concentration exceeds the sensor’s sensitivity range, first subject the seawater sample to an evaporation‑concentration pretreatment before loading it onto the DMF chip.
